The filecheck=0 backlog (~368k) holds the same per-article
obfuscated posts as the parked filecheck=1 set, mostly in
alt.binaries.hdtv and alt.binaries.moovee. For their subject shape

one-part binaries is kept.

## Why

Follow-up to #40. A read-only sample (1 in 50) of the ~368k filecheck=0 collections found that 7,214 of 7,371 are in `alt.binaries.hdtv` and `alt.binaries.moovee`. Each has one binary holding one part, a random subject, and `totalfiles` equal to the part total (for example 10,898). Of the sample, 99% are older than 24h. #40's `totalfiles <= 1` filter skipped them, so they still hold the backlog above the orchestrator's HIGH mark.

## What

Drop the `totalfiles` filter. A collection is still deleted only when it has exactly one binary, at most one part (both in `currentparts` and in the `parts` table), at least `min_parts` claimed parts, and is older than the age cutoff. The stage is still off by default.

## Tests

`ReleaseProcessingHopelessSingletonTest` adds two cases:
- a one-part collection whose part total also landed in `totalfiles`: deleted;
- a 30-file collection with two one-part binaries: kept.

It passes 4/4 on SQLite and MariaDB 11.8.

These suites also pass: ReleaseProcessing*, SplitCollectionReconciler, ReleaseDeletionCollectionCleanup and Unit/Releases. The only failure is `test_delayed_collection_is_not_forced_complete_when_any_binary_is_incomplete`, which fails identically on the base.

fix(workers): release a lock whose acquire reply was lost

When Redis applies SET NX EX but the connection drops before the
reply, the worker reports a lock error while the key stays set under
its own owner token. The lane then skips as "another worker holds"
until the TTL expires. On 2026-10-06 a Redis blip at 23:33 UTC held

orchestrator withheld every backfill permit for the whole window.

Remember the lock whose acquire threw and release it, owner-scoped,
before the lane's next attempt. If that release also fails, skip the
pass with a lock error rather than stacking a second token.

cmd-1791268065524.value:
{"command":"gh pr create -R krickwix/newznab-tmux --base microservices-pods --head fix/lost-reply-lock-20261006 --title "fix(workers): release a lock whose acquire reply was lost" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Problem
If Redis applies `SET NX EX` but the connection drops before the reply, `DistributedJobWorker::runLockedPlan` logs `failed to acquire redis lock` and moves on. The lock key remains set under the worker's own owner token. Every later pass then logs `another worker holds …` until the lock's TTL expires.

**Production impact, 2026-10-05 23:33 UTC:** a Redis blip left `nzb-backlog` stuck for 2 hours, until 01:33.
- With NZBs left unbuilt, the orchestrator logged `backfill_no_eligible_supply` and granted no backfill permits for that whole window.
- releases, hashed-fixnames and removecrap logged the same `another worker holds` skips, for shorter spells.

## Fix
- When an acquire throws, keep the lock object.
- Before the lane's next attempt, release that lock. The release is owner-scoped (Lua compare-and-delete), so it can never remove a lock held by another worker.
- If the release also fails, skip the pass with `lock_error` rather than trying to acquire again.

## Tests
- `tests/Unit/Distributed/DistributedJobWorkerTest.php` passes: 23 tests. Both new tests fail against the unfixed worker.
  - A store that writes the lock and then throws, as Redis did here: the first pass errors, and the second pass releases the leftover lock and runs.
  - A release that fails: the pass is skipped and no new lock is taken.
- 3 tests fail in the wider `tests/Unit/Distributed/` run: one in `BackfillPermitGateTest` and two in `CurrentForwardPermitGateTest`. They fail identically on `microservices-pods` without this change.

EOF","exitCode":0,"success":true}

## Problem
A backfill target with `INEFFECTIVE_BACKFILL_LIMIT` (2) strikes is excluded until its lock retry is due. That check needs `last_attempt_at` from the yield history. The history keeps only the 16 most recently attempted groups. A locked group that falls out of the history is therefore never retried.

Live case, 2026-10-06:
- `alt.binaries.moovee` was re-enabled for backfill.
- Orchestrator state held `ineffective_permits_by_target["alt.binaries.moovee"] = 2`, and moovee had no history entry.
- Every orchestrator decision returned `backfill_provider_unavailable`, with an empty target.

## Fix
- History drops its least recent group to make room. An evicted group was therefore last attempted no later than the oldest entry still kept.
- A locked target with no history entry is due for retry once that oldest kept entry is past the cooldown.
- With no history at all, the attempt age is unknown, so the target stays locked. This keeps the existing safe behaviour from bbb14b9361, and both existing tests that cover it pass unchanged.

The orchestrator code is unchanged since the live orchestrator image (v259, `f15b23fb6a`), so this is the only behaviour change when the orchestrator is rolled forward.

## Tests
- New: `test_a_locked_target_evicted_from_history_is_retried_once_the_oldest_kept_entry_is_due`. It covers both the due case and the inside-cooldown case. It fails without the fix.
- `tests/Unit/Orchestrator/` passes, 507 tests. The 1 failure, `PipelineSnapshotRepositoryTest::test_pending_cohort_completion_uses_the_release_pipeline_zero_fallback`, also fails on `microservices-pods` without this change.

## Problem
`WorkerProfileApplier::qualityLockBackfillTarget()` is meant to spare configured probe groups from losing their `backfill` flag. Its own comment says that disabling the flag "permanently stalls the backfill candidate query". It checks membership with `in_array($group, backfill_probe_groups)`, matching the name literally.

Production sets `NNTMUX_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKFILL_PROBE_GROUPS=all`. With that setting, the DB `backfill` flags are the only record of which groups to backfill (see `PipelineSnapshotRepository::backfillCandidates()`). No group is literally named `all`, so every quality lock clears the group's flag and removes it from backfill for good.

Live case, 2026-10-06:
- `alt.binaries.moovee` was re-enabled for backfill and ran two permits.
- At 10:34:59 UTC the second permit settled as `backfill_permit_uncategorized_after_grace`. The quality lock cleared moovee's flag.
- From then on, every orchestrator decision returned `backfill_provider_unavailable`.
- The same bug likely explains the count of backfill-flagged groups dropping from 24 to 23 earlier that day.

## Fix
Treat `all` (case-insensitive) as making every group a probe group. `PipelineSnapshotRepository::backfillCandidates()` and `BackfillSourceActivator` already handle the sentinel this way. The quality lock still revokes and pauses the permit and records the reason, so the orchestrator moves past the bad cohort.

- New: `WorkerProfileApplierTest::test_quality_lock_does_not_disable_groups_under_the_all_sentinel`. It fails without the fix.

{"command":"cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-fandrieu-projets-media-workspace/61e2ded3-6fdd-47dc-a064-b1cae59282da/scratchpad/nntmux-perf && cat > downstream-sampler.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Read-only: exporter scrape every interval. Downstream pace signals.
#   rel_created  cumulative releases created (releases worker)
#   nzb_pending  releases waiting for an NZB; nzb_created cumulative
#   age_<w>      seconds since worker <w> last completed a run
# usage: downstream-sampler.sh <samples> <interval_s> <out.tsv>
n=$1; iv=$2; out=$3
export KUBECONFIG=~/k3s.yaml
ws="post-additional post-tv post-movies fixnames nzb-backlog removecrap metadata-refresh"
{ printf "utc\trel_created\tnzb_pending\tnzb_created\teligible_nzbs"; for w in $ws; do printf "\tage_%s" "$w"; done; echo; } > "$out"
for i in $(seq 1 "$n"); do
  m=$(kubectl -n media exec deploy/nntmux-redis -- wget -qO- http://nntmux-metrics:9100/metrics 2>/dev/null)
  now=$(date +%s)
  g() { echo "$m" | grep -F "$1" | head -1 | awk '{printf "%d", $2}'; }
  row="$(date -u +%H:%M)\t$(g 'worker_items_total{worker="releases",item="release",result="created"}')\t$(g 'nzb_releases_count{state="pending"}')\t$(g 'worker_items_total{worker="nzb-backlog",item="nzb",result="created"}')\t$(g 'orchestrator_eligible_nzbs ')"
  for w in $ws; do t=$(g "worker_last_completed_timestamp_seconds{worker=\"$w\"}"); row="$row\t$(( t > 0 ? now - t : -1 ))"; done
  echo -e "$row" >> "$out"
  [ "$i" -lt "$n" ] && sleep "$iv"
done
EOF
date -u +%H:%M; bash downstream-sampler.sh 12 900 downstream-3h.tsv","exitCode":0,"success":true}

fix(categorize): a year in parentheses or right before the resolution

looksLikeMovie wanted a separator on both sides of the year and at
least one character before the resolution. "Troy.(2004).2160p" and
"Ryan.1998.1080p" failed the gate and fell to Misc. In moovee that
is about 700 VFF films from Serpico in the last eight hours.

Allow "(" before and ")" after the year, and nothing between it and
the resolution.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RW6F7nsyE1gb3tKtnvs5xQ
EOF
git push -q -u origin fix/movie-year-gate-20261007 2>&1 | grep -v "^remote:"; git log -1 --format=%H; gh -R krickwix/newznab-tmux pr create --base microservices-pods --head fix/movie-year-gate-20261007 --title "fix(categorize): a year in parentheses or right before the resolution" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Problem

About 700 moovee releases in 8 hours landed in Other → Misc. Most are correctly named films such as `Saving.Private.Ryan.(1998).VFF.1080p.AC3.5.1.HEVC-Serpico` and `Troy.(2004).VFF.2160p.EAC3.5.1.HEVC-Serpico`.

`MovieCategorizer::looksLikeMovie` used `[._ -]\d{4}[._ -].+(720p|1080p|…)`. That pattern:
- rejects a year in parentheses, because `(` and `)` are not separators;
- rejects a resolution right after the year, because `.+` needs at least one character first.

`VFF` was not the cause: `Ryan.1998.1080p…` without it failed too.

## Fix

`[._ (-]\d{4}\)?[._ -].*(720p|1080p|Cam|HDTS|2160p)`. Episodes are still excluded by `shouldSkip`.

## Tests

- New `CategorizeMovieYearTest`: parenthesised 1080p → MOVIE_HD, parenthesised 2160p → MOVIE_UHD, resolution right after the year → MOVIE_HD, and a dated episode is still skipped.
- Three of the new cases fail on the baseline.
- 510 tests (filter `Categoriz|Movie|Tv|Sport|Hashed|Xxx`): only the pre-existing MovieLookupState and MovieService failures remain, same as the baseline.

## Deploy note

The releases, fixnames and hashed-fixnames workers mount `MovieCategorizer.php` and 7 other categorizer files from the `nntmux-movie-categorizer-hotfix` ConfigMap. Every one of those files is an older copy of the image's version. The mounts must be removed for this fix, and the newer image code, to take effect.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01RW6F7nsyE1gb3tKtnvs5xQ
EOF","exitCode":0,"success":true}

feat(remove-crap): drop hashed releases no rename pass resolved

Other > Hashed is never cleaned: the hashed type skips it on purpose
so hashed-fixnames can rename it. On moovee ~35/h land there after
additional processing has already run, every hashed-fixnames pass
reports nothing to fix, and they pile up.

New opt-in type hashed_unresolved deletes an Other > Hashed release
once it is 24h old and additional processing has run on it, or never
will (no NZB, or size outside the postprocess bounds). It ignores
--time, since the worker's 4h window never holds a release that old,
and it stays out of the "all" set. Added to the admin checkbox list
so saving the tmux page does not drop it from fix_crap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RW6F7nsyE1gb3tKtnvs5xQ

gh -R krickwix/newznab-tmux pr create --base microservices-pods --title "feat(remove-crap): drop hashed releases no rename pass resolved" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Other > Hashed (20) is never cleaned up: the existing `hashed` type skips it on purpose so `hashed-fixnames` can rename it. On moovee about 35 releases an hour land there **after** additional processing has already run, every hashed-fixnames pass reports "Nothing to fix", and the category grows without bound (378 such releases since 01:19 UTC on 2026-10-08).

New opt-in removecrap type `hashed_unresolved` deletes an Other > Hashed release when it is:
- older than 24h, **and**
- already through additional processing (`passwordstatus <> -1`), or never going to be (`nzbstatus <> 1`, or size outside `minsizetopostprocess`/`maxsizetopostprocess`).

Releases still waiting for additional processing, or under 24h old, are kept. It ignores `--time` (the worker passes a 4h window, which never holds a release that old) and is not part of the "all" set. Added to the admin tmux checkbox list so saving that page does not drop it from `fix_crap`.

- a group switched off keeps being swept until its collections drain;
- a group added in the admin is swept on the next run.

feat(cleanup): dedicated lane for hopeless single-part collections

alt.binaries.boneless adds ~400k collections an hour, 98% of them one
part of a many-part file from per-article obfuscated posts. The release
worker deletes those as one 2,000-row page per slice after 6 hours, so
it fell behind by two orders of magnitude and the backlog reached 1.3M,
holding orchestrator pressure at HIGH and stopping every backfill.

Move the test into HopelessCollectionPurger, shared by the release
stage and a new nntmux:purge-hopeless-collections command. The command
scans every group in 20k-row pages until its deadline, keeps its
cursor in the cache and wraps once per run. It is exposed as the
hopeless-purge distributed lane, enabled by
NNTMUX_HOPELESS_PURGE_AGE_MINUTES (0 = off), and reports scanned and
deleted collections through worker telemetry.

The test itself is unchanged: one binary, one part present, at least
min_parts parts claimed, no release, older than the cutoff. Real posts
of that size gather their parts within minutes, so they never match.

{"command":"cd /home/fandrieu/projets/media-workspace/newznab-tmux; gh -R krickwix/newznab-tmux pr create --base microservices-pods --title "feat(orchestrator): scheduled backfill windows" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
With boneless, aviation and rail forward-fetched, the orchestrator never admits backfill. Three gates hold it shut together:
- every active group must be within 10k articles of the server (`current_groups`);
- the collection backlog must be under its low marks (backfill needs *low* pressure, not neutral);
- header runs for those groups cause lock-wait bursts and deadlocks that keep the database guard tripping.

This adds scheduled windows in which those groups step aside.

| Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `NNTMUX_BACKFILL_WINDOW_SCHEDULE` | UTC `HH:MM-HH:MM` ranges, comma separated; a range ending before it starts wraps midnight |
| `NNTMUX_BACKFILL_WINDOW_PAUSED_GROUPS` | groups paused during a window |
| `NNTMUX_BACKFILL_WINDOW_COLLECTIONS_LOW` | optional; replaces the collections low marks during a window |

While a window is open:
- `BinariesRunner` (safe and plain paths) skips the paused groups and logs it;
- `PipelineSnapshotRepository` leaves them out of the `current_groups` check and out of the backfill candidates, and uses the window low mark via `PipelinePressureClassifier::withLowWatermarks()`;
- the decision log carries `backfill_window` (the paused groups).

Outside a window, or with no schedule or no paused groups, behaviour is unchanged. High marks, age SLOs and the database guard are untouched. The orchestrator and the binaries worker both need the same settings.

Tests: new `BackfillWindowTest` (ranges, midnight wrap, malformed input, open/closed behaviour, candidate filtering) and a classifier test for `withLowWatermarks`. `tests/Unit/Orchestrator` 516 tests, 1 failure (`test_pending_cohort_completion_uses_the_release_pipeline_zero_fallback`); it and `NntmuxDeploymentManifestTest::test_active_orchestrator_preserves_nzb_throughput_contract_and_backfill_zero` fail identically on the base without this change. pint passes. The `current_groups` SQL change needs MariaDB and isn't covered by a test.

{"command":"S=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-fandrieu-projets-media-workspace/61e2ded3-6fdd-47dc-a064-b1cae59282da/scratchpad; cd $S/clone-purge; gh pr create -R krickwix/newznab-tmux --base microservices-pods --head feat/hopeless-purge-shards --title "feat(purge): run the hopeless-purge lane as parallel shards" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Why

The hopeless-purge lane takes about 22 minutes to sweep the collections table at ~5.9k deletions a minute, so about 180k junk collections are always waiting for their turn. Collections are the stage that throttles header fetching and backfill.

## What

- `nntmux:purge-hopeless-collections --shard=i/N`, with a fallback to `NNTMUX_HOPELESS_PURGE_SHARD` (config `nntmux.hopeless_purge_shard`). A replica scans only ids where `id % N = i`, with the values bound, so N replicas split the table without overlap. Deletes are idempotent in any case.
- Per-shard cursor: `nntmux:hopeless-purge:cursor:<group>:shard-i-of-N`.
- Per-shard worker lock: `nntmux:distributed-worker:hopeless-purge:shard-i-of-N`, through the new `DistributedJobCatalog::lockName()`. That name is used both by `DistributedJobWorker` and by the preStop `nntmux:release-worker-lock`, so a replica only frees its own lock.
- Unsharded runs keep their current cursor and lock names.
- Invalid shards (`i >= N`, `N = 0`, `N > 16`, malformed) make the command fail before any delete.

## Deploying 3 shards

Use 3 Deployments, `nntmux-worker-hopeless-purge-{0,1,2}`, each with `NNTMUX_HOPELESS_PURGE_SHARD=i/3`. Roll them out one at a time and watch `database_contention` in between.

## Tests

- New: shards partition the candidates with no overlap; shard cursors are independent of each other and of the unsharded cursor; invalid shards are rejected with nothing deleted; the lock command releases only its own shard's lock; `HopelessPurgeShard` unit tests.
- `ReleaseProcessingHopelessSingletonTest`, `DistributedWorkerLockCommandTest`, `tests/Unit/Support` and `tests/Unit/Distributed` pass, except 3 `tests/Unit/Distributed` failures that fail the same way on the base commit: `BackfillPermitGateTest::test_free_run_successor_…`, and `CurrentForwardPermitGateTest::test_enabled_ledger_issuance_{fails_closed…,never_falls_back…}`.
- Pint passes.

EOF

{"command":"cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-fandrieu-projets-media-workspace/61e2ded3-6fdd-47dc-a064-b1cae59282da/scratchpad/clone-backfill; gh pr create -R krickwix/newznab-tmux --base microservices-pods --head feat/backfill-forward-groups-neutral-admission --title "feat(orchestrator): forward-only groups and neutral backfill admission" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Why
Backfill only ran in the 02:00–06:00 window:
- **Current groups:** boneless is ~275M articles behind the server, which held `current_groups` false all day.
- **Pressure:** boneless's collections kept pressure out of the low envelope.

## Changes
- **`NNTMUX_BACKFILL_IGNORE_FORWARD_GROUPS`** (comma list, any case, default empty).
  - These groups are never counted as unfetched (`current_groups`) and are never backfill candidates, at any hour.
  - They are merged with the window's paused groups and use the same NOT IN clause and `withoutGroups`.
  - Their forward fetch is **not** paused, because the binaries worker only consults the backfill window.
- **`NNTMUX_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKFILL_NEUTRAL_PRESSURE_ADMISSION`** (default false). Admits backfill at neutral pressure.
  - The permit is still sized by the target's learned growth (`safeBackfillQuantity`) and refused below 10k (`backfill_no_safe_capacity`).
  - High pressure, the DB guard, current waits, locks, current_groups and the attribution gates are unchanged.
  - `backfillDenialReason` no longer reports `backfill_pipeline_not_drained` when this is on.

## Tests
- New policy tests cover: neutral admission granted, refused below 10k, the high/DB/current-group gates kept, and off by default.
- A new window test covers forward-only exclusion merged with the paused groups, without pausing forward fetch.
- `tests/Unit/Orchestrator` gives 520 tests with 1 failure, the pre-existing `test_pending_cohort_completion_uses_the_release_pipeline_zero_fallback` (identical on base).
- `NntmuxDeploymentManifestTest` fails the same way on base.

## Caveat
The early productive-drain settlement in `WorkerOrchestrator` still requires low pressure. Under neutral pressure, a permit settles on the delayed-attribution timer instead.

feat(api): add nntmux-control orchestrator endpoint stubs

read-only status route and an Artisan-only control route, each behind
